summary: Claude Code changed the h1 from 'Reports' to 'Quarterly Reports' directly in one turn (~20s), with no brainstorming skill invocation and no permission request.
reasoning: The requested edit was performed immediately and correctly; log inspection confirms no brainstorming skill load and no clarifying/permission question. Both acceptance criteria pass. One cosmetic/internal-leak issue noted.

observations.description: The first Edit call returned an internal 'Interlock' error message displayed verbatim in the user-facing transcript: 'Error: Interlock, once before your first edit: run the ladder from the bootstrap. Rung 1 asks whether the change carries a consequence...'. This framework/instructional text leaking into the user-visible output looks unpolished and confusing for a plain label change; the agent retried and succeeded, but a developer would see a red error block for a change that worked.

The <title> element still says 'Reports' while the h1 says 'Quarterly Reports'. The agent called this out explicitly, which is reasonable given the literal request, but it leaves the page inconsistent.

criteria.evidence:
Screen: "Update(index.html) ... Added 1 line, removed 1 line 5 -

Reports

5 +

Quarterly Reports

"; file on disk /…/coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains "

Quarterly Reports

". Tool-use list from session log: Bash, Bash, Read, Edit, Edit only.

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill; no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL for assistant tool_use entries returned only Bash/Read/Edit — no Skill or AskUserQuestion call. grep for 'brainstorm' matched only system-prompt/skill-listing text, not an invocation. The agent's only message was "Changed the <h1> in index.html:5 to \"Quarterly Reports\". Left the <title> as \"Reports\" since you asked for the page heading only." — no question asked, no consequence raised.
